No. The evidence does not show a loss of 67.7 ha after the cut-off date. The 67.7 ha loss is recorded in 2020, before the 2020-12-31 baseline, so it falls outside the 2021–2025 period you asked about.

For 2021–2025, no tree-cover loss event of 0.5 ha or more was detected anywhere in the 2,843.1 ha property, and the satellite data covered the whole asset. The only post-baseline loss was 0.4 ha in 2021, in patches too small to count as events.

Some limits apply. Changes under 0.5 ha, at edges, or narrower than the 30 m pixels may be missed. The result also says nothing about EUDR compliance or about anything outside 2021–2025. The data runs through 2025, and the JRC 2020 map shows no forest on the property in 2020.
